O.outcome_detail: Conceptual problem performance on isomorphic original problems

result.effect: Phi coefficient maximized at five attempts; McNemar test nonsignificant beyond three attempts

cells.quote: For the original conceptual question, the phi coefficient increases as more attempts are considered on the quiz up until five attempts. The McNemar’s test statistic also reaches a minimum at five attempts and the test results are not significant beyond three attempts. Examining the correlation matrix revealed that the quiz was harder than the exam when less than five attempts were considered, and the two assessments reaches a balance at five or more attempts.
cells.note: The study reports association and balance between assessment performances, not a randomized causal effect.

O.outcome_detail: Conceptual problem performance on transfer problems

result.effect: Phi approximately 0.2 across attempts; McNemar statistic minimized at two attempts

cells.quote: For the transfer problem, the phi coefficient remains roughly the same for all attempts at around 0.2, with all correlation statistically significant at α = 0.01 level. The McNemar’s χ2 statistic has a minimum at attempt two, and the McNemar’s test is significant at α = 0.01 level for all other attempts. Examining the correlation matrix revealed that the quiz performance is better than the exam performance.
cells.note: The transfer problems used the same knowledge components in a similar format but were not included in the open problem banks.

O.outcome_detail: Numerical problem performance on isomorphic original problems

result.effect: Phi coefficient maximized at two attempts; McNemar test significant beyond one attempt

cells.quote: The phi coefficient is maximized when two quiz attempts are being considered, meaning that students’ performance on the quiz is most similar to the exam, if we only consider their first two attempts. The association with the transfer numerical problem is weaker than that of the conceptual problems. All correlations are significant at α = 0.01 level according to chi-square test, except for attempts six and seven for transfer problem, which are significant at α = 0.05 level. However, the McNemar’s test shows that the two assessments are unbalanced when more than one attempt is considered. Examining the correlation matrix shows that when more than one quiz attempt is allowed, it is easier to answer the numerical question correct on the quiz than on the exam.
cells.note: The positive direction reflects higher quiz correctness than exam correctness after more than one attempt, not a randomized treatment effect.
